gloss: just a moment ago; only a short while ago

definitions.gloss: just a moment ago; only a short while ago
definitions.explanation: Refers to a point in time only minutes before the present. つい emphasizes that very little time has passed; {先|さき}ほど is a polite word for 'a little while ago.'

examples.japanese: つい{先|さき}ほど{帰|かえ}ってきた。
examples.english: I got back just a moment ago.

examples.japanese: その{件|けん}はつい{先|さき}ほど{連絡|れんらく}を{受|う}けた。
examples.english: I was informed of that matter just a short while ago.

examples.japanese: つい{先|さき}ほどまでここにいたのに、{彼|かれ}はもう{姿|すがた}が{見|み}えない。
examples.english: He was here just a moment ago, yet he is already nowhere to be seen.

notes:
Combines つい ('just; barely') with {先|さき}ほど ('a little while ago') to stress that the event happened only minutes before now. More polite and slightly more formal than さっき.

POSITION IN SENTENCE:
Appears before the verb or at the start of the sentence.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- さっき: a little while ago — casual, everyday speech
- {先|さき}ほど: a little while ago — polite and neutral; つい adds the 'only just' nuance
- たった{今|いま}: just now — even more immediate, 'this very moment'
